It argues that deep responsibility is not limited to the moral, and that attributability and accountability are independent, not two levels. Accountability may need nothing metaphysically robust. Limits: the positive view is offered as a hunch, the psychopath is a stipulated case, and the lecture does not restate the Reason View of Freedom Within Reason ([LIT-685](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-685.md)). |

Reviews Allport's contact hypothesis (equal status, common goals, cooperation, authority support) and names four problems: selection bias in cross-sectional studies, conditions that are facilitating rather than essential, no account of process, and no account of how effects generalize. A meta-analysis of 515 studies (713 independent samples) finds that intergroup contact typically reduces intergroup prejudice. The effect does not appear to come from participant selection or publication bias, the more rigorous studies show larger effects, and the effects typically generalize to the whole outgroup and across targets and settings. Allport's optimal conditions enhance the effect but work as a bundle and are not essential to it. | Deferred — filed 2026-10-23, not read. Participants won money in a concept-formation task; afterwards one group was asked by the experimenter to return it as a personal favour (he was paying out of his own pocket), one was asked by a departmental secretary on behalf of the psychology department, and one was not asked. Those who did the experimenter a personal favour rated him most likable. Standardly read as a dissonance effect: one justifies a favour by liking its recipient. | Deferred — filed 2026-10-23, not read. | [LIT-1428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1428.md) | Psychopathy as a Clinical and Empirical Construct | Hare & Neumann (2008), Annual Review of Clinical Psychology 4:217–246. The PCL-R's items form four correlated factors, Interpersonal, Affective, Lifestyle and Antisocial, explained by one superordinate factor; psychopathy is dimensional, and no component, affective or antisocial, is more essential than the others. Cleckley's Clinical Profile, drawn from an unrepresentative sample, should not be the test of the construct. | Active — read 2026-10-23 ([NOTE-1094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1094.md)): in full, from the copy Hare posts on his own site. Worth reading as the authors' own statement of what the construct is, made while defending it against the charge that the PCL-R has "drifted" from Cleckley. The PCL-R's 20 items fall, 18 of them, into four correlated factors: Interpersonal and Affective (together Factor 1) and Lifestyle and Antisocial (together Factor 2). A single superordinate factor explains them, and the authors hold that no component, the affective one included, is more essential than the others. That is the sharpest constraint the record has on borrowing only the affective features of psychopathy for a corporation. Hare receives royalties from the PCL-R. |
